title: A three-hop gossip chain
summary: Mira tells Tom who Leo's father was. Tom tells Ines, saying it came from Mira. Ines tells Rook, garbled: she drops the reef and invents a poisoning. Each listener should know it from the one who told them, and Rook should hold the garbled version, not the true one. Mira's other news stops at Tom.

father.label: what Leo's father did on the Halcyon
father.truth: Leo's father was second mate on the Halcyon, and his hand on the wheel put her onto the Gannet Teeth.

garble.label: the garbled story about Leo's father
garble.truth: (false) Leo's father was the Halcyon's cook and poisoned the crew with bilge-salt in their stew.

automatic.label: the Board's plans for the light
automatic.truth: The Lighthouse Board will replace Mira with an automatic lamp in the spring.

spine.scene: Saltmere Light, the keeper's kitchen, morning

spine.text: Morning in the keeper's kitchen at Saltmere Light. The kettle ticks on the stove. Tom has rowed out with the post, and it's only him and his sister on the rock.
Letters, a coal bill, and something from the Board with a seal on it. You look like you slept in the lamp.
Didn't sleep. Sit down.

spine.hint: Tom jokes about the Board's letter and the price of coal.

spine.text: *She breaks the Board's seal and reads.* They're putting in an automatic lamp come spring. No keeper.
They can't. Mira, this rock is you.
They can. Keep it under your hat. I'll not have the Bell pitying me.

spine.hint: Tom swears to keep his sister's news to himself; Mira changes the subject to the newcomer.

spine.text: The new one. Leo. I went through the Halcyon papers again. His father was second mate on her that night. His hand on the wheel put her on the Gannet Teeth.
The newcomer's da? God. Does he know?
He knows something. Not that. Don't you dare tell him, or anyone.

spine.hint: Tom presses Mira on how sure she is; Mira answers in as few words as she can.

spine.text: *He pockets the coal bill and gets up.* I'll say nothing. Tide's turning, I'd best row back.

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, the kitchen behind the bar, noon

spine.text: Noon at the Drowned Bell. Ines has Tom cornered in the kitchen behind the bar, peeling potatoes, with the door shut on the empty taproom.
You've a face like a man holding a hot coal, Tom Voss. Out with it.
It's nothing. Family.

spine.hint: Ines works on Tom the way she always does, with flattery and potatoes.

spine.text: *He lowers his voice.* Swear on the Bell. Mira says the new one's father was second mate on the Halcyon. Says he ran her onto the Gannet Teeth.
No. That nice boy? Oh, love, that's a cruel thing to carry.
That's all you get. Not a word about anything else up at the light.

spine.hint: Ines promises discretion, which she has never once managed; Tom already regrets telling her.

spine.text: Tom slips out the back door toward the harbor. Ines finishes the potatoes alone, thinking.

spine.hint: Ines talks to herself about the newcomer while she works.

spine.text: Afternoon on the quay. Rook sits mending nets in the lee of the fish shed. Ines comes down with his dinner in a covered pot, and stays to talk.
Your dinner, and don't say I never feed you.
Aye. Thank you.

spine.hint: Ines makes small talk about the weather while she works up to her news.

spine.text: You'll not believe what Tom told me. The newcomer's father was the cook on the Halcyon. The one who put bilge-salt in the crew's stew, Tom says. Poisoned half of them before she ever struck.
*He stops mending.* Poisoned. Aye. I heard men were sick that night.

spine.hint: Rook turns the story over; he is slow to judge and quick to remember.

spine.text: Not a word to the boy, mind.
I don't talk to boys.

spine.hint: Ines gets ready to go back up to the Bell; Rook is left with the story and his nets.

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, the taproom, evening

spine.text: Evening at the Drowned Bell. Leo sits at the bar with a letter he keeps unfolding and folding. Rook has his corner by the fire. Tom comes in late and won't meet anyone's eye.
Ines, is there anyone in town who sailed on the Halcyon and lived?
*Too brightly.* Oh, love, that was long ago. More stew?

spine.hint: Everyone at the bar is careful around Leo, each for their own reasons.

spine.text: Everyone goes quiet when I say her name.
Names have weight. Hers more than most.

spine.hint: Rook looks at Leo a long time; Tom tries to lighten the mood with a story about something else.

probe.ask: Ines, what's the talk in town about my family?
Rook, what do people say my father did?
Tom, what has Mira told you about my father?
Ines, what will become of the light come spring?
Rook, is the keeper's job safe, do you think?
Tom, is your sister's place at the light safe?

spine.text: *He stands.* I've nets to see to. Night, all.
Was it something I said?
Tom's always running off. Don't mind him.

spine.hint: Ines and Rook exchange a look neither of them explains to Leo.

spine.text: I'll find someone who'll talk to me. There must be someone.
Try the chapel graves. Dead talk plenty, if you listen.

spine.hint: Rook says something about the Halcyon's dead; Ines hushes him.

spine.text: Leo goes up to his room. The taproom empties until only Ines and Rook are left with the fire.

spine.hint: Alone, Ines and Rook go over what Tom said, each with the version they have.

spine.text: Sleep, Ines. Story'll keep till morning.

spine.hint: Ines banks the fire and says goodnight.

probe.ask: Rook, how did the newcomer's father come to be blamed for the wreck?
Mira, who was my father on the Halcyon?
